comment: CANONICAL debugger-side trace bring-up catalog (bkpt-packages/trace-support). Consumers bundle a snapshot at build/dev time (the ViewAlyzer app never fetches at runtime; a future app fetch would come from this repo). Offline user override: <userAppData>/ViewAlyzer/trace-support.json (same shape). Rows group parts sharing a vendor debug-domain map. Device ID allowlists identify the known parts in each group; an arbitrary nonzero value at the same address is not sufficient vendor identification. Unknown IDs require catalog validation before vendor-specific initialization is enabled. Its init ops then run through a read-modify-write interpreter: {addr, set} = write literal, {addr, or} = OR bits in, {addr, insert, mask} = (old & ~mask) | (insert & mask). The token $prescaler normally resolves to (cpu-clock-hz / swo-freq-hz) - 1. A row-level swo_clock_div makes both the probe receiver and $prescaler use cpu-clock-hz / swo_clock_div; an individual op may override that with src-clock-div. tpiu:false means the row replaces the standard ARM TPIU programming (parts with their own SWO block). Optional per-row keys: onchip = the vacore_capture --probeless profile token for the family (Auto chip selection in the on-chip trace flow; absent = generic discovery), note = a one-line caveat logged when the row matches (for example: SWO bring-up not catalogued for this family yet). Rows are probed IN ORDER and the first match wins; keep more specific layouts before broader groups.

access_prep.comment: DBGMCU_CR: D1/D3 debug clocks and trace clock, enabled with read-modify-write. Do not write the reset value back: on H723 that write gates the live debug domain even when zero was read before preparation.

route.comment: Bench-proven end to end on NUCLEO-H723ZG with the native BKPT server: multi-AP discovery, arm, wrapped RRD drain, and OpenCSD decode. The live ROM walk and TMC DEVID still determine whether an ETF exists and its capacity.

SWTF LAR unlock
SWO LAR unlock
SWO SPPR: async NRZ (replaces the standard TPIU block)
SWO CODR: traceclkin/core follows RCC SWS, D1CPRE and PLL1 P/R; requires stm32h7-rcc clock-model support.

RCC AHB4ENR: GPIOB clock (SWO pin = PB3)
GPIOB MODER: PB3 alternate function
GPIOB OSPEEDR: PB3 very high speed
GPIOB AFRL: PB3 AF0 (TRACESWO)

devices.name: stm32n6

rom_roots.comment: Architected Armv8-M PPB ROM root. Runtime component IDs remain authoritative.

access_prep.comment: RIFSC RIMC_ATTR0: ETR master 0 needs MCID1|MSEC|MPRIV or AXI writes are acknowledged and silently discarded.

route.comment: Verified on STM32N6570-DK over bkpt_probe direct SWD with the ELF-reserved 4 KiB ETR ring: input 0 wrapped with 4096 captured bytes (3920 nonzero); input 1 produced 32 bytes (1 nonzero). The diagnostic restored all trace routing/state and used no OpenOCD runtime.

allowed_regions.comment: Verified clocked AXISRAM2 window above the boot ROM stack. This is a safety boundary, not proof that an arbitrary firmware leaves it unused.

quirks.comment: Set TRCPDCR.PU before programming the Cortex-M55 ETM.
Program TRCCONFIGR=1; reset state enables conditional trace packets unsupported by the packaged decoder.
Initialize RRP/RWP to the resolved buffer base before every circular arm.
An ETR AXI memory error can wedge AP1; disarm immediately and require a power cycle rather than retrying.

init.comment: DBGMCU_CR DBGCLKEN + TRACECLKEN on AP0: enable the debug clock and export the dedicated TPIU clock to the system trace output.
CSTF funnel LAR unlock

CSTF funnel CTRL: enable ONLY slave port 0 (ITM), clearing any other slave (insert+mask, so a prior session's slave 1 cannot stick). The SWV/SWO path carries ITM+DWT only; enabling slave 1 lets the M55 ETM flood the pin with ETMv4 trace the SWV decoder cannot parse and starves the ITM stimulus FIFO (bench 2026-08-29: recorder stuck in ITM_WaitReady, 0 events decoded). ETM belongs to the ETR path (capture/probeless/st_n6.tcl).
ETF (TMC) LAR unlock
ETF CTL: disable before reconfiguring
ETF MODE: hardware FIFO (pass the ATB stream downstream to the replicator)
ETF FFCR: formatter bypassed (one source; the SWV receiver wants the raw ITM stream)
ETF CTL: TraceCaptEn
replicator LAR unlock
replicator IDFILTER0: pass all IDs (branch 0)
replicator IDFILTER1: pass all IDs (branch 1 -> SWO/TPIU)
SWO block LAR unlock
SWO SPPR: async NRZ (the core-private TPIU does not exist on this part; the 0xE008A000 system SWO block replaces it)
SWO FFCR: no formatting (raw ITM stream), TrigIn passthrough

SWO CODR: baud divider. STM32N6 feeds the TPIU clock from the CPU clock source through its fixed divide-by-8 branch, so the divider is (cpu/8)/swo-1. At the DK workload's 600 MHz CPU clock the SWO source is 75 MHz.

devices.note: STM32N6: ITM/SWO rides the system trace tree (CSTF funnel -> ETF in FIFO passthrough -> replicator -> SWO block at 0xE008A000). DBGMCU (DEV_ID, trace clocks) is on AP0; the core and the whole trace tree are on AP1 (the default AP). The ETR path (probeless on-chip trace) shares the funnel + ETF; see capture/probeless/st_n6.tcl.
devices.comment: Keep this specific layout before broader groups; 0xE0044000 aliases a nonzero word on this part.

match.comment: STM32C562RE: CubeProgrammer device ID 0x44E on NUCLEO-C562RE; ST STM32C5 DFP stm32c562xx.h maps DBGMCU to AHB3 + 0x4000 (0x44024000). Core debug uses AP1. Use system AP0 for DBGMCU: AP1 reads these registers as zero while the core sleeps.

init.comment: DBGMCU_CR: TRACE_EN bit 5, TRACE_IOEN bit 4, DBG_STOP/STANDBY bits 1/2. Standard ARM TPIU handles async SWO; preserve other debug state.

match.comment: DBGMCU as seen from the Cortex-M33 core AP (AP1 on H5); AP0 aliases it at 0xE0044000 but the products program through the core AP. dev_id 0x474 = H503 (verified on the rack 2026-08-28: IDCODE 0x10036474), 0x484 = H56x/H573.

init.comment: DBGMCU_CR: TRACE_EN + TRACE_IOEN + DBG_STOP/STANDBY, TRACE_MODE=00 async SWO (same bit layout as the U5/L5 generation; RM0492 DBGMCU_CR). Without TRACE_EN the TPIU is absent from the bus.

match.comment: DBGMCU for U3/U5/L5/WBA; H5 uses its own row. IDs from ST's STM32CubeCLT 1.19.0 Programmer Data_Base device records: U3=454, U535/545=455, L5=472, U5F/G=476, U59/A=481, U575/585=482, WBA5=492, WBA6=4B0. Never match an arbitrary nonzero word: RW612 reads 0x003 at this address on the bench. Unknown IDs require catalog validation; they retain generic Cortex-M debugging.

init.comment: DBGMCU_CR: TRACE_EN (trace clock gate — without it the TPIU is absent from the bus: accesses bus-fault AND wedge the ST-LINK DAP until probe power-cycle) + TRACE_IOEN + DBG_STOP/STANDBY; TRACE_MODE=00 async SWO

match.comment: Known F0/F1/F2/F3/F4/F7/L0/L1/L4/G0/G4/C0/U0/WB/WL IDs from ST's STM32CubeCLT 1.19.0 Programmer Data_Base. H7/H5/N6 and TrustZone-M33 layouts have separate rows. An ID list is a necessary guard, not a trace-capability claim: the core's discovery still gates every feature. Unknown/non-ST IDs do not authorize writes to this vendor register map.

init.comment: DBGMCU_CR: TRACE_IOEN + DBG_SLEEP/STOP/STANDBY (keeps trace clocked through WFI idles)
